staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this preserved vulnerable checkout. Its `HTMLparser.c`, `parserInternals.c`, `buf.c`, and `xmlstring.c` line map matches the saved patch and crash traces for the misplaced HTML DOCTYPE -> `htmlParseSystemLiteral()` -> `xmlStrndup()` path.

classification.classification_note: The saved crash is an AddressSanitizer global-buffer-overflow READ in `xmlStrndup()`. Source analysis closes the source-level chain as follows: `htmlParseSystemLiteral()` saves `startPosition` relative to the current `BASE_PTR`, the vulnerable pre-copy `NEXT` enters `xmlNextChar()`'s low-lookahead path, buffered-input growth rebases `ctxt->input->base` via `xmlBufSetInputBaseCur()`, and the caller then reconstructs `BASE_PTR + startPosition` only after that rebase. `xmlStrndup()` trusts the resulting `cur` and `len`. The saved runtime artifacts disagree on the reported read size, so `access_size` remains null and this GT does not assert an exact copied byte count at the sink.

bug_description.original: A global-buffer-overflow (out-of-bounds read) occurs in xmlStrndup (xmlstring.c) when invoked from the HTML parser (HTMLparser.c) during DOCTYPE/system/public literal parsing (e.g., htmlParseSystemLiteral/htmlParseDocTypeDecl). The parser can supply an incorrect length/offset to xmlStrndup, causing it to read past the end of a buffer into adjacent global memory. This can crash the process and may lead to memory corruption or information disclosure.
bug_description.normalized: The staged witness is the exact 75-byte file at `gt_results/secbench_oss_libxml2.ossfuzz-42522712/poc`, whose load-bearing substring is `<!DOCTYPEs SYSTEM" ">`. Content parsing reaches the misplaced-DOCTYPE branch, `htmlParseExternalID()` takes the `SYSTEM` arm, and `htmlParseSystemLiteral()` saves `startPosition` immediately after the opening quote and counts the one-byte literal body. The vulnerable closing-quote `NEXT` runs before `xmlStrndup((BASE_PTR + startPosition), len)`. In buffered-input parsing, `xmlNextChar()` first checks `ctxt->input->end - ctxt->input->cur < INPUT_CHUNK`; when that path calls `xmlParserGrow()`, `xmlBufSetInputBaseCur()` rewrites `ctxt->input->base` to the current buffer start while preserving only the cursor offset. `htmlParseSystemLiteral()` then rebuilds the copy source from the rebased `BASE_PTR` plus the stale pre-grow `startPosition`, and `xmlStrndup()`'s `memcpy()` performs the observed out-of-bounds read.

source.description: First vulnerability-relevant project statement. After the attacker-controlled misplaced DOCTYPE has selected the `SYSTEM` literal parser, this line materializes the literal start as an offset relative to the current input-buffer base, and that offset becomes the stale value later recombined with a rebased `BASE_PTR`.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` has sha256 `9a484b45c866e92c0c9deb959c540dd3037733d8e84d0dee5144c7225ad4c743`. Its bytes at offsets `0x1e..0x32` contain `<!DOCTYPEs SYSTEM" ">`, so `htmlParseSystemLiteral()` is entered on the exact one-byte system literal `" "` and records the start offset from that attacker-controlled layout here.

sink.description: Crash sink. `xmlStrndup()` trusts the caller-provided `cur` and `len`, and this `memcpy()` performs the saved AddressSanitizer out-of-bounds read from global parser memory.

root_cause.description: Root cause fixed by the patch. `htmlParseSystemLiteral()` advances past the closing quote before duplicating the literal bytes. If that advance enters the input-growth path, later code recombines the old `startPosition` with a rebased `BASE_PTR`. The patch removes this pre-copy advance by moving `NEXT` after `xmlStrndup()`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The literal parser converts the attacker-controlled system-literal location into a buffer-relative offset here. That saved offset remains the basis of the later copy source even if buffered-input growth rewrites `BASE_PTR` before `xmlStrndup()` is called.

parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific gate. After earlier content in the witness, the parser sees the exact misplaced `<!DOCTYPE` introducer in content and recognizes it as a DOCTYPE declaration rather than a comment or bogus markup.

coarse_trace.summary: The staged witness reaches the misplaced-DOCTYPE branch, and DOCTYPE parsing takes the attacker-controlled `SYSTEM` external-identifier arm.
The parser records the system literal's start offset relative to `BASE_PTR` and counts the exact one-byte literal body.

The vulnerable pre-copy `NEXT` enters the low-lookahead growth path, and buffered-input growth rewrites `ctxt->input->base` to the current buffer start without updating the already-saved literal offset.
After the rebase, `htmlParseSystemLiteral()` reconstructs `BASE_PTR + startPosition` and passes that stale pointer together with `len` to `xmlStrndup()`.
The stale pointer/length pair reaches `xmlStrndup()`, whose `memcpy()` matches the saved AddressSanitizer global-buffer-overflow read.

fine_trace.note: The attacker-controlled bytes `SYSTEM" "` in the misplaced DOCTYPE satisfy this branch, so the parser chooses the `SYSTEM` external-identifier path and enters `htmlParseSystemLiteral()` on the exact one-byte literal from the witness.

Source. Immediately after consuming the opening quote, the parser materializes the system literal start as an offset relative to the current input-buffer base. This saved offset is later reused to build the `xmlStrndup()` source pointer.
The loop counts the literal body bytes before the closing quote. For the staged witness the body is exactly one space byte, so this step leaves `len == 1` when parsing reaches the terminating quote.

Root cause. After the loop stops on the closing quote, this pre-copy `NEXT` calls `xmlNextChar(ctxt)` before the literal bytes are duplicated, leaving the saved `startPosition` live across later parser-input maintenance.

The vulnerable `NEXT` first tests whether less than `INPUT_CHUNK` lookahead remains. The saved witness is only 75 bytes long, so buffered parsing of this literal necessarily reaches the closing quote with this predicate true; the public default crash trace confirms a buffered `htmlReadFile()` path, and the Stage 01 reproducer confirms the same sink without a symbolized caller-side state snapshot.

Because the low-lookahead branch is taken, `xmlParserGrow()` refreshes the buffered input and re-applies parser pointers relative to the current buffer content. It preserves only `curBase`, the cursor offset from the old base, not the separately saved literal-start offset `startPosition` from step 2.

This is the concrete rebasing step: the parser input base is rewritten to the start of the current buffer (`base` is passed as `0` by step 6). `startPosition` is not adjusted here, so the old literal-relative offset no longer matches the new `BASE_PTR`.

After the rebase, the caller reconstructs the copy source pointer from the new `BASE_PTR` plus the stale `startPosition`, and pairs it with the previously counted `len`. That is the bad `xmlStrndup(cur, len)` argument construction fixed by moving `NEXT` after the copy.

Sink. `xmlStrndup()` copies from the caller-provided `cur` for the caller-provided `len` with no bounds validation. The saved AddressSanitizer traces place the crash at this `memcpy()` and report a global-buffer-overflow read into parser global storage near empty-string literals in `parserInternals.c`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch is source-consistent with the root cause because it moves `NEXT` after `xmlStrndup()` in both `htmlParseSystemLiteral()` and `htmlParsePubidLiteral()`, but Stage 02 did not execute the fixed build and therefore does not claim dynamic confirmation.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced the crash with `ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0 ./fuzz/html /gt/poc`, producing `AddressSanitizer: global-buffer-overflow` in `xmlStrndup` at `xmlstring.c:53`.

format.name: Malformed HTML byte stream with misplaced DOCTYPE `SYSTEM` literal
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact staged witness at `gt_results/secbench_oss_libxml2.ossfuzz-42522712/poc`. Its load-bearing property is the malformed substring `<!DOCTYPEs SYSTEM" ">` inside ordinary HTML content, parsed through a buffered HTML path that reaches `htmlParseSystemLiteral()` on the one-byte literal `" "` and then executes the vulnerable closing-quote `NEXT` before `xmlStrndup()`. No broader input class, byte-count range, or exact sink read size is claimed here.
